# AEO content optimization for AI search visibility

Curated by Skill Harbor — @bencium's AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) skill: optimize content for AI citations, not traditional search rankings. Core principles: the 18-token extraction rule (key claims must be self-contained, quotable sentences needing zero surrounding context), single-topic focus pages (focused URLs beat comprehensive guides), citations plus statistics (verifiable data, methodology, collection date, expert attribution), and freshness (most AI citations come from content updated in the last 10 months). The skill walks the agent through the authority-level strategy (challengers optimize aggressively; established sites keep a light touch — over-optimizing a rank-1 site can lose visibility), then what to generate: a 50-word dated product overview, 15 FAQs with JSON-LD schema (30-50 word answers, persistent anchor IDs), evidence panels (claim, methodology, data source, date, limitations), JSON-LD schema blocks (FAQPage, HowTo, Product, Organization), an anti-pattern list (keyword stuffing, vague hedged language, multi-topic guides, FAQ answers over 50 words, buried answers), a 0-10 scoring framework (extraction, focus, authority, freshness), an implementation checklist, and a testing protocol (ask ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini "What is X?", "Compare X to Y", "What's the best…", then track mentions, links, accuracy, quoted evidence). Honest caveats: claims like "30-40% more visibility" and the Princeton findings are the skill author's — treat them as marketing lore, not...
